web-tech-001.question: Which of the following correctly lists the elements in the first line (the request line) of an HTTP/1.1 request?
choices: The method, the request target (such as a path) and the HTTP version
The HTTP version, the status code and a short reason phrase
The source IP address, the destination port number and the method
web-tech-001.explanation: An HTTP request consists of the request line, the headers (one "Name: value" per line), a blank line and the body, in that order. For example, "GET /docs/index.html HTTP/1.1" is a line that requests /docs/index.html with the GET method. In HTTP/1.1 the Host header must also be sent, so that the server can tell which site a request is for even when several sites are run on the same IP address. The first line of a response is the status line, which lists the version, the status code and the reason phrase, as in "HTTP/1.1 200 OK".
choiceNotes: Correct. For example, "GET /docs/index.html HTTP/1.1".
These are the elements of the first line of a response (the status line).
The IP address is carried in the IP header and the port number in the TCP header; they are not part of the HTTP request line.

web-tech-002.question: Among HTTP methods, which of the following is not "safe" (not intended to change the state of resources on the server) but is "idempotent" (sending the same request any number of times leaves the same state as sending it once)?
choices: GET
POST
PUT
web-tech-002.explanation: GET and HEAD are safe methods that only read resources, and safe methods are also idempotent. PUT replaces the state of the specified resource with the content sent, so sending it any number of times gives the same result as sending it once: it is idempotent but not safe. DELETE is likewise idempotent. POST may create a new order or post each time it is sent, so it is generally not idempotent, and PATCH is not necessarily idempotent either. An idempotent request has the advantage that it can simply be resent when a communication failure leaves the result unknown, with little risk of problems.
choiceNotes: GET only reads resources, so it is both safe and idempotent.
POST may create a new resource each time it is sent, so it is generally neither safe nor idempotent.
Correct. PUT replaces the resource with the content sent, so any number of sends leaves the same state.

web-tech-003.question: Which of the following correctly pairs an HTTP status code with its meaning?
choices: 301: The requested resource is temporarily at another URL
404: The requested resource was not found on the server
503: The request was malformed and the server could not understand it
web-tech-003.explanation: A status code is a three-digit number whose hundreds digit indicates its class. 2xx is success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 3xx is redirection (301 Moved Permanently, 302 Found, 304 Not Modified), 4xx is a client error (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found) and 5xx is a server error (500 Internal Server Error, 503 Service Unavailable). 404 indicates that the resource identified by the URL was not found on the server.
choiceNotes: 301 indicates that the resource has moved permanently. 302 or 307 is used for a temporary move.
Correct. 404 Not Found indicates that the requested resource was not found.
A malformed request is indicated by 400 Bad Request. 503 indicates that the server temporarily cannot handle requests because of overload or maintenance.

web-tech-004.question: On a members-only website, an ordinary member who is logged in requests a page that only administrators may access. The server knows who the user is but does not allow access to this page. Which of the following status codes is most appropriate to return?
choices: 401 Unauthorized
403 Forbidden
404 Not Found
web-tech-004.explanation: 403 Forbidden indicates that the server understood the request but refuses to allow access. Despite its name, 401 Unauthorized is the code for missing or invalid authentication information, and the WWW-Authenticate header tells the client how to authenticate. Here the server has confirmed who the user is and what is lacking is permission (authorization), so 403 applies. Some designs deliberately return 404 to avoid revealing that an admin page exists, but the code that describes the situation as it is is 403.
choiceNotes: 401 is used when authentication information is missing or invalid. This user has already authenticated.
Correct. It indicates that the user is authenticated but lacks permission.
404 indicates that the resource was not found. Some designs use it to hide a page's existence, but the code that describes the situation as it is is 403.

web-tech-005.question: A web API returns data in JSON format as the body of its response. Which of the following headers is generally added to the response to indicate the format of the body?
choices: Accept: application/json
Content-Type: text/html
Content-Type: application/json
web-tech-005.explanation: The kind of data in the body is indicated by the Content-Type header, whose value is a media type (MIME type) in the form "type/subtype", such as text/html or image/png. The media type of JSON is application/json. JSON is a text format that represents data with name-value pairs and arrays, as in {"id": 42, "tags": ["a", "b"]}; it is more concise than XML and easy to handle from JavaScript, so it is widely used in web APIs. The Accept header is used in a request to tell the server which formats the client wants to receive.
choiceNotes: Accept is a request header that tells the server which formats the client wants to receive. The format of a response body is indicated by Content-Type.
text/html indicates that the body is an HTML document. JSON uses application/json.
Correct. The media type of JSON is application/json.

web-tech-006.question: A browser requests an image it received earlier once again, putting the ETag value from that earlier response into the If-None-Match header. If the image on the server has not changed, which of the following is the correct server response?
choices: 200 OK, sending the whole image body again even though it is the same as before
304 Not Modified with no body, and the browser uses the image it has stored
404 Not Found, making the browser delete its stored old image and fetch it again
web-tech-006.explanation: An ETag is an identifier that represents a particular version of a resource. The browser puts the ETag into If-None-Match to send a conditional request meaning "send it if it has changed since this version", and if it has not changed, the server returns 304 Not Modified without a body. This takes only the one round trip for the check, and the image data does not have to be sent again. If it has changed, the server returns 200 OK with the new body and a new ETag. Within the period set by max-age in Cache-Control, the browser uses its stored copy without even this check.
choiceNotes: The image has not changed, so the body need not be sent again. Avoiding that is the purpose of a conditional request.
Correct. 304 means "it has not changed, so the stored copy may be used".
404 is the code for a resource that was not found, but the image exists.

web-tech-007.question: Which of the following correctly describes HTTP/2 and HTTP/3?
choices: HTTP/2 can handle several requests in parallel over one TCP connection, but a packet loss can make other streams wait too; HTTP/3 reduces this with QUIC over UDP
HTTP/2 uses messages in the same text format as HTTP/1.1 and opens a new TCP connection in parallel for each request, so that several resources can be received at once
HTTP/3 runs over TCP like HTTP/2 and only changes the header compression method; the effect of packet loss is the same as in HTTP/2, and it does not use UDP
web-tech-007.explanation: Even HTTP/1.1 can reuse one TCP connection with persistent connections (keep-alive), but responses on one connection are received one at a time in order, so browsers opened several connections in parallel. HTTP/2 splits messages into binary frames and multiplexes several streams over one TCP connection so they are sent in parallel. However, because TCP delivers its byte stream in order, when a single packet is lost, data of unrelated streams must also wait until the retransmission arrives (head-of-line blocking). HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which runs over UDP and manages ordering per stream, so the effect of a loss stays within that stream.
choiceNotes: Correct. HTTP/2 can send in parallel by multiplexing, but a loss in TCP affects all streams. HTTP/3 reduced this with QUIC.
HTTP/2 uses binary frames and multiplexes several requests over one connection. Opening new connections is actually slower.
HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which runs over UDP, not TCP.

web-tech-008.question: From a web server with an RTT of 40 ms, one HTML file and the four images it references are fetched one after another. Assume that establishing a TCP connection takes one round trip and each request and response take one round trip, and ignore data transfer time, server processing time, TLS and connection teardown. Which of the following is the difference in total time between opening a new TCP connection for each object and reusing one TCP connection (a persistent connection)?
choices: 160 ms
200 ms
400 ms
web-tech-008.explanation: There are five objects in total. With a new connection each time, each object takes two round trips, one for connection setup and one for the request and response, giving 5 × 2 × 40 = 400 ms. With a persistent connection, the connection is set up only once at the start, followed by just the five requests and responses, giving (1 + 5) × 40 = 240 ms. The difference is 400 − 240 = 160 ms, which is the four connection setups saved. In HTTP/1.1, persistent connections are the default behavior.
choiceNotes: Correct. 400 − 240 = 160 ms; four connection setups are saved.
This takes the five connection setups, 5 × 40 = 200 ms, as the difference. Even a persistent connection needs one connection setup at the start.
This is the total time when connecting each time, 5 × 2 × 40 = 400 ms, not the difference.

web-tech-009.question: HTTP is a stateless protocol. Which of the following correctly describes what this means together with the usual way a website keeps a user logged in?
choices: The server remembers every request that arrived on the same TCP connection, so the user stays logged in as long as the browser does not close the connection
HTTP itself has a mechanism that records logged-in users, so the web application does not need to do anything to keep state
HTTP itself does not remember how requests relate to each other, so a session ID issued by the server is passed in a cookie, which the browser sends back each time
web-tech-009.explanation: Stateless means that each request is handled independently and the protocol does not remember the contents of earlier requests. Because the server does not need to keep state, any server can handle a request, which has the advantage of making it easy to add servers. To keep state such as a login, the server passes a session ID with the Set-Cookie header, and the browser automatically attaches it in the Cookie header to requests to the same site. Using the ID it receives, the server looks up the user information (the session) stored on its own side.
choiceNotes: Reusing a TCP connection and remembering a login are different things. Connections can be closed midway, and HTTP does not remember earlier requests even on the same connection.
HTTP itself does not record login state, so the application manages it with cookies or tokens.
Correct. Passing a session ID in a cookie ties requests to the user.

web-tech-010.question: Which of the following correctly describes the cookie set by the header above?
web-tech-010.code: Set-Cookie: sid=8f3a2c9d; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
choices: Because of the Secure attribute, the cookie value is stored encrypted in the browser and cannot be read by other applications
Because of the HttpOnly attribute, the page's JavaScript cannot read this cookie
Because of SameSite=Lax, this cookie is not attached even to requests sent from pages within the same site
web-tech-010.explanation: A cookie with the Secure attribute is sent only over HTTPS. With the HttpOnly attribute, the page's JavaScript cannot read it through document.cookie and the like, which reduces the damage if a session ID would otherwise be stolen through XSS. The SameSite attribute decides whether the cookie is attached to requests started from other sites; with Lax it is attached to GET navigations that follow a link from another site, but not to form POSTs from other sites or to image loads. A cookie without an expiry set by Expires or Max-Age generally becomes a session cookie that is deleted when the browser is closed.
choiceNotes: Secure is an attribute that makes the cookie be sent only over HTTPS; it does not encrypt the stored value.
Correct. An HttpOnly cookie cannot be read by scripts, which reduces the damage from theft through XSS.
SameSite decides whether the cookie is attached to requests started from other sites; it is attached to requests within the same site.

web-tech-011.question: Which of the following correctly describes a difference between the browser's localStorage and cookies?
choices: localStorage data is not attached to requests automatically; the JavaScript of pages of the same origin reads and writes it
localStorage data, like cookies, is put into a header and sent to the server automatically with every request to the same site
localStorage can also be given the HttpOnly attribute, so even if a session ID is stored there, the page's scripts cannot read it
web-tech-011.explanation: localStorage is a storage area in the browser that keeps string keys and values per origin; it has no way to set an expiry and generally remains until deleted. It is not sent to the server automatically, so to send it, JavaScript puts it into a request. Cookies are small, generally up to about 4 KB each, and are sent automatically with every request, whereas larger data can be kept in localStorage. However, the page's JavaScript can read it at any time, so if there is an XSS flaw its contents can be stolen. This risk must be considered when storing values used for authentication.
choiceNotes: Correct. localStorage data is not sent automatically; scripts of the same origin read and write it.
Cookies are what is attached to requests automatically. localStorage data is not sent automatically.
HttpOnly is a cookie attribute. Scripts of the same origin can always read the contents of localStorage.

web-tech-012.question: Three application servers are placed behind a load balancer, which distributes requests to them in turn (round robin). The session information of a logged-in user is stored only in the memory of the server that handled the login. Which of the following is an appropriate pair of a likely problem and its countermeasure?
choices: When a request goes to another server, the session is not found and the user appears to be logged out. Keep sessions in a shared store that all servers can use
The three servers issue the same session ID separately and the IDs collide. Make session IDs short sequential numbers so that users can remember them
The load balancer cannot read cookies, so HTTPS stops working. Stop encrypting the traffic between the load balancer and the servers
web-tech-012.explanation: If session information exists only in one server's memory, a server that receives the next request cannot identify the user when the request is distributed to it. One countermeasure is to keep sessions in a shared store that every server can read and write (an in-memory data store or a database). Another is session persistence (sticky sessions), which keeps sending the same user's requests to the same server, but sessions are lost if that server stops and the load also tends to become uneven. Keeping servers stateless makes it easy to add or remove servers.
choiceNotes: Correct. With a shared store, every server can use the same session.
Session IDs are made long enough and random so that they cannot be guessed. Making them short increases the risk of impersonation.
The session problem has nothing to do with HTTPS. Stopping encryption only lowers security.

web-tech-013.question: Which of the following correctly describes a typical signed JWT (JSON Web Token)?
choices: The payload is encrypted with the signing key, so passwords or credit card numbers put in it cannot be read along the way
Even after a token has expired, the server must accept it as long as the signature is valid, because it has not been tampered with
It consists of a header, a payload and a signature, each encoded with Base64URL and joined with "."; the signature detects tampering, but the contents are not encrypted
web-tech-013.explanation: A JWT has three parts, "header.payload.signature": the header holds the signature algorithm (for example HS256), and the payload holds information (claims) such as the user identifier and the expiry (exp). The signature is made from the header and payload with a secret key, so a server that receives the token can confirm that the contents have not been tampered with and who issued it. However, Base64URL is not encryption, and anyone can decode and read it, so no secret information is put in it. When sent to an API, the token is generally placed after Authorization: Bearer.
choiceNotes: The payload of a signed JWT is only encoded and can be read by anyone. Secret information is not put in it.
Along with the signature, the server checks the expiry (exp) and rejects expired tokens.
Correct. The signature detects tampering, but the contents are not encrypted.

web-tech-014.question: A photo-printing app, with the user's permission, reads the user's photos stored on another company's photo storage service. In OAuth 2.0, which of the following roles shows the user a screen asking for permission and, when the user agrees, issues an access token to the app?
choices: Resource server
Authorization server
Client
web-tech-014.explanation: OAuth 2.0 has four roles: the resource owner (the user), the client (the photo-printing app), the authorization server and the resource server (the API that returns the photos). The authorization server confirms the user and obtains consent, then issues the client an access token limited in scope and lifetime. The client calls the resource server's API with the token, and the resource server checks the token and returns the photos. The user does not have to give the app the password for the photo storage service and can also revoke the permission later.
choiceNotes: The resource server is the side that checks the token and returns the resources (the photos). Tokens are issued by the authorization server.
Correct. It obtains the user's consent and issues the access token.
The client is the side that receives the token and calls the API (the photo-printing app).

web-tech-015.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect?
choices: OAuth 2.0 is a mechanism for delegating permission to access resources (authorization), and OpenID Connect builds on it by adding an ID token that conveys the result of authentication, so that it can be used for login
OAuth 2.0 is a mechanism for conveying the result of user authentication, and OpenID Connect does not use it but sends the user's password directly to each connected service to check it
OpenID Connect is a protocol for encrypting HTTP communication and is used instead of TLS when sending login screens
web-tech-015.explanation: An OAuth 2.0 access token represents permission, meaning "you may use resources within this scope", and is not designed to confirm who has logged in. OpenID Connect adds to the OAuth 2.0 flow an ID token in the form of a signed JWT. The ID token contains the issuer, the user identifier, the intended client, the expiry and so on, and the client checks the signature and contents to learn who the user is. This mechanism is used for features that let users log in with an account from another service and for single sign-on.
choiceNotes: Correct. It adds an ID token that conveys the result of authentication to OAuth 2.0, which is an authorization mechanism.
The roles are reversed. OAuth 2.0 is an authorization mechanism, and OpenID Connect is built on top of OAuth 2.0.
Encrypting communication is the role of TLS. OpenID Connect is used over communication protected by TLS.

web-tech-016.question: Which of the following is an appropriate web API design that follows the principles of REST?
choices: Put the operation name into the URL, as in /getUser?id=42 or /deleteUser?id=42, and send everything with GET
Represent a user resource with a URL such as /users/42 and express operations with HTTP methods, such as GET to retrieve and DELETE to delete
Have the server remember each client's earlier requests, so that the next request only sends a short command that depends on them
web-tech-016.explanation: In REST, the things being handled are represented as resources identified by URLs, and operations on them are expressed with HTTP methods such as GET (retrieve), POST (create), PUT or PATCH (update) and DELETE (delete). For example, GET /users/42 retrieves a resource, and when POST /users creates a new user, the server returns 201 Created with the URL of the new resource. Each request is made stateless, containing all the information needed to process it. If an operation such as deletion is done with GET, data may be lost merely because a browser fetches links in advance or a crawler visits.
choiceNotes: Putting operation names into URLs differs from the REST approach. Also, deleting with GET risks unintended execution, for example when links are fetched in advance.
Correct. Resources are expressed with URLs and operations with HTTP methods.
In REST each request is independent, and the design is stateless so the server does not rely on earlier requests.

web-tech-017.question: A browser opens https://www.example.com:8443/docs/guide.html?lang=ja#install. Which part of this URL is not included in the request sent to the server and is used only inside the browser after the page loads?
choices: ?lang=ja
#install
web-tech-017.explanation: This URL consists of the scheme (https), the host name (www.example.com), the port number (8443; if omitted, 443 for https), the path (/docs/guide.html), the query (lang=ja) and the fragment (install). The browser uses the port number to decide where to connect and sends the path and query to the server in the request, but it does not send the fragment after #. The fragment is used only inside the browser, for example to move to the position of the element with id="install" in the page.
choiceNotes: The port number is used to decide where to connect, and a non-default port number is also included in the Host header.
The query is sent to the server in the request together with the path and is used, for example, as conditions for the server's processing.
Correct. The fragment is not sent to the server; the browser uses it to indicate a position in the page and the like.

web-tech-018.question: To put the Japanese character "あ" into a URL query, the byte sequence representing it in UTF-8 (E3 81 82) is percent-encoded. Which of the following is the correct result?
web-tech-018.explanation: In percent-encoding, when characters that cannot be written in a URL as they are, or characters with special meanings such as / ? # &, are used as data, the characters are turned into bytes and each byte is written as "%" followed by two hexadecimal digits. "あ" is the three bytes E3 81 82 in UTF-8, so it becomes %E3%81%82. A space becomes %20 (in the form submission format, + is also used). In JavaScript, the encodeURIComponent function performs this conversion.
choiceNotes: Correct. Each of the three bytes is written in the form %XX.
This notation uses the Unicode code point (U+3042) and is what JavaScript's old escape function outputs, but it is not a standard notation for URLs.
This is a character reference, the HTML notation for writing a character by its number; it is not URL percent-encoding.

web-tech-019.question: A chat app needs to deliver new messages from the server to the browser immediately. Which of the following correctly describes WebSocket?
choices: A method in which the browser sends an HTTP request every few seconds and asks the server each time whether new messages have arrived
It switches a connection started with HTTP (an upgrade) so that either the server or the browser can send messages over that one connection
A method in which, when an event occurs, a server notifies another server's pre-registered URL with an HTTP POST request
web-tech-019.explanation: WebSocket asks for Upgrade: websocket in an HTTP request, and when the server returns 101 Switching Protocols, the same TCP connection is switched to WebSocket communication. After that the connection is kept open, and either the server or the browser can send small messages with little overhead. With a method that asks at fixed intervals, requests occur even when there is nothing new, and new messages are delayed by up to the interval between checks. Notifying from server to server with an HTTP POST is called a webhook.
choiceNotes: This is a method of asking periodically (polling). Requests occur even when there is nothing new, and delays of up to the interval arise.
Correct. The connection stays open, and messages can be sent in both directions at any time.
This describes a webhook. It is used for notifications between servers.

web-tech-020.question: A merchant's server wants to know immediately when a payment is completed on an online payment service. Which of the following correctly describes the method in which the payment service sends a notification by HTTP POST to a URL the merchant registered in advance (a webhook)?
choices: The merchant does not need to ask the payment service at fixed intervals, and notifications arrive only when something changes. Whether a notification is genuine is checked with a signature or similar means
The merchant's server does not need to accept requests from outside, so the URL that receives notifications does not have to be exposed on the internet
Notifications arrive over a WebSocket connection opened with a browser, so the merchant's staff must always keep a browser open
web-tech-020.explanation: With a webhook, the service where an event occurred notifies the receiver by sending an HTTP request to the URL the receiver registered. Compared with the receiver repeatedly asking about the state, there are no wasted requests and changes are learned immediately. In return, the receiver must accept requests arriving from the internet, so it checks whether a notification is genuine, for example with a signature made with a shared secret key. Failed notifications may be resent, so they are processed in such a way that receiving the same notification twice causes no problem.
choiceNotes: Correct. Notifications arrive only when something changes, and the sender is verified with a signature or similar means.
Notifications arrive from outside as HTTP requests, so the receiving URL must be exposed.
Webhooks are notifications between servers and do not use browsers or WebSocket.

web-tech-021.question: Which of the following correctly describes the DOM (Document Object Model) used in browsers?
choices: A form into which the table structure of a server's database is converted, as HTML tables (table elements), to be sent to the browser
A representation of an HTML document as a tree whose nodes are elements and so on, which JavaScript can read and write
A format in which CSS rules are compressed by removing whitespace, to make files smaller and load faster
web-tech-021.explanation: The browser parses HTML and builds a tree structure (the DOM tree) whose root is the html element and whose nodes include head, body and the paragraphs inside them. JavaScript changes the page through the DOM, finding elements with document.querySelector, rewriting text and attributes, and adding elements. When the DOM changes, the browser redoes the layout calculation and painting as needed. The DOM is standardized as an interface for manipulating documents that does not depend on any particular programming language.
choiceNotes: The DOM is the structure of the document inside the browser and has nothing to do with databases.
Correct. It represents the document as a tree so that scripts can manipulate it.
It has nothing to do with compressing CSS. The structure built from CSS is called the CSSOM.

web-tech-022.question: For the element styled with the CSS above, which of the following is the width from the outer edge of the left border to the outer edge of the right border?
choices: 200px
224px
264px
web-tech-022.explanation: In the CSS box model, an element consists of the content, the padding, the border and the margin, layered from the inside out. With box-sizing: content-box (the default), width is the width of the content only, so the width to the outside of the border is 200 + 10 × 2 + 2 × 2 = 224px. The margin is the space outside the border and forms the gap to other elements. With box-sizing: border-box, width includes everything up to the border, and the content width becomes 200 − 24 = 176px.
choiceNotes: This is the content width only. With content-box, the padding and border are added outside width.
This also adds the left and right margins, 20 × 2 = 40px. The margin is the space outside the border.

web-tech-023.question: Assume there are no other style specifications. In the HTML above, which of the following is the color of the text "Hello"?
web-tech-023.code: Hello
choices: Red
Green
Blue
web-tech-023.explanation: When several rules apply to the same element, the rule whose selector has the higher specificity wins. Specificity is compared as the tuple (number of IDs, number of classes, attributes and pseudo-classes, number of elements): #main p is (1, 0, 1), while .content p and p.note are both (0, 1, 1), so the red of #main p, which contains an ID, is used. Between rules of equal specificity, the one written later wins. A declaration written directly in the style attribute, or one marked !important, takes precedence over these.
choiceNotes: Correct. #main p, which contains an ID, has the highest specificity, (1, 0, 1).
The specificity of .content p is (0, 1, 1), lower than the rule containing an ID. It is also written before p.note, which has the same specificity.
p.note is written last, but its specificity (0, 1, 1) is lower than the rule containing an ID, so it is not used. Without the ID rule, the text would be blue.

web-tech-024.question: In the processing a browser does before showing the first screen (the critical rendering path), a <script src="app.js"> written without attributes inside <head> makes the HTML parser stop at that point. Which of the following correctly describes the behavior when the defer attribute is added to this element?
choices: It is executed immediately as soon as the download finishes, stopping the HTML parser, and the execution order of multiple scripts is not guaranteed
It is neither downloaded nor executed, and is loaded only when the user first interacts with the page
It is downloaded while the HTML parser keeps working and executed after the document has been parsed, in the order written in the document
web-tech-024.explanation: The browser parses HTML to build the DOM and CSS to build the CSSOM, combines the two to decide what to draw, calculates the positions and sizes of elements (layout) and then draws them (paint). A script element without attributes may rewrite the DOM, so the HTML parser stops until the script has been downloaded and executed. With defer, the download proceeds while the parser keeps working, and execution happens after the whole document has been parsed, in the order written in the document. With async, a script runs as soon as its download finishes, so the order is not guaranteed.
choiceNotes: This is the behavior of the async attribute. With defer, scripts run after the document has been parsed, in the order written.
Even with defer, the script is downloaded right away and executed without waiting for user interaction.
Correct. It is downloaded without stopping the parser and executed after the document has been parsed, in the order written.

web-tech-025.question: When the JavaScript above is run in a browser, which of the following is the order in which the characters are shown on the console?
choices: A → B → C → D
A → D → B → C
A → D → C → B
web-tech-025.explanation: A page's JavaScript runs on a single main thread, and no other work cuts in until the currently running code finishes. First, all the synchronous code runs, showing A and D. The function passed to the Promise's then runs as a microtask immediately after the current code finishes, so C is shown next. Even with 0 ms given to setTimeout, its function is put into the queue as a task, and the event loop takes it out only after the microtasks are done, so B comes last.
choiceNotes: Functions passed to setTimeout or then are not run on the spot; they run after the synchronous code finishes.
Promise callbacks (microtasks) run before setTimeout callbacks (tasks).
Correct. The order is the synchronous A and D, then the microtask C, then the task B.

web-tech-026.question: Under the browser's same-origin policy, which of the following URLs is considered to have the same origin as https://www.example.com/app/index.html?
choices: https://www.example.com/data/list.json
http://www.example.com/app/data.json
https://api.example.com/app/data.json
web-tech-026.explanation: An origin is determined by the combination of three things, the scheme, the host name and the port number, and two URLs have the same origin only when all three match. The path does not matter, so /data/list.json has the same origin. Under the same-origin policy, a page's JavaScript in principle cannot read the contents of responses received from other origins. This prevents a malicious page's script from reading information from other sites where the user is logged in.
choiceNotes: Correct. The scheme, host name and port number (443) are the same; only the path differs.
The scheme differs (http), and the default port number also becomes 80, so it is a different origin.
The host name differs (api.example.com), so it is a different origin even though it is under the same domain.

web-tech-027.question: JavaScript on a page at https://app.example.com uses fetch to send a POST request with a body of Content-Type application/json to https://api.example.net/orders. Which of the following correctly describes how CORS behaves in this case?
choices: CORS also works outside browsers, so without the server's permission even a POST sent from a command-line tool is stopped along the network
The browser first sends a preliminary check (a preflight) with the OPTIONS method, and sends the actual POST only if the server returns permission in its headers
Requests to a different origin are always sent without any check, and the page's JavaScript can read the response even if the server adds nothing to it
web-tech-027.explanation: CORS is a mechanism that allows requests to other origins, and the reading of their responses, which the same-origin policy restricts, within the scope the server permits. A POST with Content-Type application/json is a kind of request that a simple form submission cannot produce, so the browser first uses OPTIONS to state the method and headers it will use and asks for permission. If the server's response does not grant permission with headers such as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, the browser does not send the actual request. CORS is a rule enforced by the browser, so the server must protect itself separately with authentication and permission checks.
choiceNotes: CORS is a check performed by browsers and does not stop requests from tools other than browsers. Server-side authentication and permission checks are needed separately.
Correct. For a POST with an application/json body, permission is confirmed with a preflight before sending.
Scripts can read responses from other origins only when the server permits it with headers such as Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

web-tech-028.question: Which of the following correctly describes a Service Worker?
choices: A program that keeps running on a web server and handles database queries in response to requests from browsers
A CSS feature for speeding up drawing by rewriting the page's DOM directly, which can also be used on pages that are not HTTPS
A script that runs inside the browser separately from the page, can intercept the page's requests and return stored responses, and is used for offline display
web-tech-028.explanation: A Service Worker is a script registered by a page that runs inside the browser separately from the page. It receives the requests made by pages of its origin (the fetch event) and can decide in script whether to send them to the network or to return a stored response. With it, pages can be shown even offline and push notifications can be received. Because it has the powerful ability to intercept communication, it can be used only on HTTPS pages (and on localhost for development), and it cannot touch the DOM directly.
choiceNotes: Application servers and the like run on servers; a Service Worker runs inside the browser.
A Service Worker is a script written in JavaScript, and it cannot touch the DOM directly.
Correct. It intercepts the page's requests and is used for offline display with stored responses and similar purposes.

web-tech-029.question: For a page with responsive design that also supports smartphones, which of the following is the main purpose of writing <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> in <head>?
choices: To make the width used for laying out the page match the device's screen width and display it without shrinking
To have the server automatically regenerate images to match the resolution of the device's screen
To display the page only in PC browsers and refuse access from smartphones
web-tech-029.explanation: Without this setting, a smartphone browser lays out the page at a wide width that assumes a page designed for PCs (generally around 980px) and then shrinks it to fit on the screen. width=device-width makes the layout width match the device's screen width, and initial-scale=1 sets the initial zoom to 100%. On top of that, CSS media queries (for example @media (max-width: 600px)) switch the layout and text size according to the screen width.
choiceNotes: Correct. It makes the layout width match the screen width and displays the page at a zoom level that does not shrink it.
To have a browser choose an image that fits the screen, the srcset attribute of the img element and the like are used. The viewport setting does not make the server generate images.
The viewport setting decides the display width and zoom; it has no function for refusing access.

web-tech-030.question: The response for a "my page" whose content differs for each user is given Cache-Control: private, max-age=60. Which of the following correctly describes the effect of this setting?
choices: Only shared caches such as a CDN reuse it for 60 seconds, and the user's browser cache does not store it
The browser cache can reuse it as is for 60 seconds, but shared caches such as a CDN or a proxy do not store it
It is not stored in any cache, so even the browser fetches it from the server again every time
web-tech-030.explanation: A browser cache is used by a single user only, whereas the caches of a CDN or a proxy are shared by many users. private indicates that the response must not be stored in shared caches, and max-age=60 indicates that for 60 seconds after storing, it may be used without checking with the server. If per-user pages were stored in a CDN, it could lead to accidents in which other users are shown someone else's information. To have a response stored nowhere, no-store is used, and to allow storing but require a check with the server on each use, no-cache is used.
choiceNotes: private prevents storage in shared caches; it is the user's browser cache that can store it.
Correct. The browser can use it for 60 seconds without checking with the server, but shared caches do not store it.
The setting that prevents storage anywhere is no-store. With private, the response is stored in the browser cache.

web-tech-031.question: When a web server compresses responses with gzip or Brotli before sending them, which of the following generally gains the least reduction in transferred data from compression?
choices: An HTML file
A JavaScript file
A JPEG photo
web-tech-031.explanation: The browser states the compression methods it supports with the Accept-Encoding header, and the server indicates the method it used in the compressed response with the Content-Encoding header. Text such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript and JSON contains repeated character sequences, so compression makes it much smaller. Images in JPEG, PNG or WebP, and videos, are already compressed formats, so compressing them again hardly makes them smaller and wastes processing time. For this reason, servers are generally configured to compress only text responses.
choiceNotes: HTML is text in which the same tags and words appear repeatedly, so it compresses well.
JavaScript is also text, and compression is very effective for it.
Correct. JPEG is already a compressed format, so compressing it again hardly makes it smaller.

web-tech-032.question: 1.5 MB of text data is compressed with gzip to one third of its size and sent. The bandwidth is 10 Mbps and the RTT is 100 ms, and before the data starts to be sent, the TCP connection, the TLS handshake and the HTTP request take three round trips in total. Assume 1 MB = 10^6 bytes, and ignore compression and decompression time, headers and waiting caused by TCP congestion control. Which of the following is closest to the time until all the data has been received?
choices: About 0.4 s
About 0.7 s
About 1.5 s
web-tech-032.explanation: The compressed size is 1.5 ÷ 3 = 0.5 MB, which is 0.5 × 8 = 4 Mbit. Sending this at 10 Mbps takes 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4 s, and adding the 3 × 0.1 = 0.3 s of the three round trips before sending begins gives about 0.7 s in total. Without compression, transferring 1.5 MB = 12 Mbit takes 12 ÷ 10 = 1.2 s, for a total of about 1.5 s.
choiceNotes: This is only the 0.4 s of data transfer, without adding the 0.3 s of the three round trips before sending begins.
This is 1.2 + 0.3 = 1.5 s, for sending the 1.5 MB without compression.

web-tech-033.question: A CDN receives 2,000 requests per second, and its cache hit ratio rises from 90% to 98%. The response time is 20 ms on a hit, and 200 ms on a miss because the content is fetched from the origin server and returned; only requests that miss reach the origin server. Which of the following is the combination of the number of requests reaching the origin server and the average response time after the ratio reaches 98%?
choices: 40 per second, about 24 ms
40 per second, about 110 ms
160 per second, about 24 ms
web-tech-033.explanation: The requests that miss are 100 − 98 = 2% of the total, so 2,000 × 0.02 = 40 per second reach the origin server. At 90% it was 200 per second, so a rise of just 8 points in the hit ratio cuts the origin server's load to one fifth. The average response time is 0.98 × 20 + 0.02 × 200 = 19.6 + 4 = 23.6 ms, about 24 ms. This is also much shorter than the 0.9 × 20 + 0.1 × 200 = 38 ms at 90%.
choiceNotes: This takes the response time as the simple average of 20 ms and 200 ms, (20 + 200) ÷ 2 = 110 ms. The average must be weighted by the proportions of hits and misses.
160 is the decrease in requests reaching the origin server, 200 − 40. The number reaching it after the ratio reaches 98% is 40.

web-tech-034.question: Among Core Web Vitals, the metrics of a web page's user experience, which of the following does CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) represent?
choices: The time until the largest image or block of text on the screen is displayed while the page loads
The delay from a user's click or key press until its result is drawn on the screen
The amount by which elements unexpectedly shift position during display, caused for example by images or ads that load later
web-tech-034.explanation: Core Web Vitals consist of three metrics: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) for loading speed, INP (Interaction to Next Paint) for responsiveness to interaction, and CLS for visual stability (INP replaced FID in March 2024). CLS quantifies unexpected shifts in position, such as text being pushed down by images or ads that appear later. Specifying width and height for images and videos so that their space is reserved in advance makes CLS smaller.
choiceNotes: This is LCP, the metric for loading speed.
This is INP, the metric for responsiveness to interaction.
Correct. CLS represents visual stability, that is, unexpected layout shifts.

web-tech-035.question: Which of the following is an appropriate pairing of an image format for web pages with its typical use?
choices: A logo with a transparent background: JPEG. It can store transparent areas as they are
A landscape photo: PNG. Because it is lossless, it is always smaller than JPEG for photos
A company logo or icons: SVG. Because it describes shapes with coordinates and formulas, it does not blur when enlarged
web-tech-035.explanation: JPEG uses lossy compression and can make photos small, but it cannot handle transparent areas. PNG uses lossless compression and can handle transparency, and suits images with crisp text and lines, but for photos it is generally much larger than JPEG. SVG is a vector format that describes shapes as XML text, so it displays smoothly at any size and suits logos and icons. WebP and AVIF support both lossy and lossless compression and transparency, and can generally be smaller than JPEG or PNG at the same quality.
choiceNotes: JPEG cannot handle transparent areas. When transparency is needed, PNG, WebP, SVG or the like is used.
PNG is lossless, so for photos it is generally larger than JPEG.
Correct. SVG is a vector format, so it does not blur however much it is enlarged.

web-tech-036.question: 3,000 bytes of image data are encoded with Base64 and embedded in HTML. If no line breaks are inserted, which of the following is the number of characters after encoding?
choices: 2,250 characters
4,000 characters
6,000 characters
web-tech-036.explanation: Base64 splits every 3 bytes (24 bits) into four 6-bit groups and represents each with one of 64 characters. The size therefore becomes 4/3 of the original, 3,000 ÷ 3 × 4 = 4,000 characters. When the number of original bytes is not a multiple of 3, "=" is added at the end to fill out a 4-character unit. Embedding an image in HTML or CSS reduces the number of requests, but the data becomes about 33% larger, and the browser can no longer store it as a separate file and reuse it.
choiceNotes: This multiplies by 3/4 instead of 4/3.
Correct. 3,000 ÷ 3 × 4 = 4,000 characters.
This is the number of characters when each byte is written as two hexadecimal characters.

web-tech-037.question: A web system is built in three tiers: a web server, an application server and a database server. Which of the following is the processing that the application server mainly handles?
choices: It receives user input, performs business processing such as checking logins and registering orders, and produces results using the database
It accepts HTTP requests from browsers and returns unchanging files such as images and CSS as they are
It stores data in the form of tables and searches or updates it in response to SQL queries from applications
web-tech-037.explanation: In a three-tier setup, the web server accepts HTTP requests from users, returns static files and passes requests that need processing to the application server. The application server performs business processing in programs and leaves reading and writing of data to the database server. Separating the roles makes it possible to scale up each tier separately and to place the database where it cannot be reached directly from outside. In small systems, one computer may handle several tiers.
choiceNotes: Correct. It performs the business processing and produces results using data obtained from the database.
This is the main role of the web server.
This is the role of the database server.

web-tech-038.question: Which of the following correctly describes a reverse proxy?
choices: When PCs in a company view sites on the internet, it connects to outside servers on their behalf and records or restricts browsing
It performs, on the user's behalf, the queries that convert domain names to IP addresses, starting from the root servers, and keeps the results for a while
It is placed in front of web servers, receives users' requests on their behalf, relays them to the servers behind it and handles TLS processing and the like
web-tech-038.explanation: A reverse proxy is placed on the server side, receives requests from users and relays them to one or more servers behind it. It takes on roles such as performing HTTPS encryption in one place (TLS termination), storing and returning frequently used responses and distributing requests over several servers, and it can also hide the configuration of the servers behind it from users. What connects to the outside on behalf of users in a company is a forward proxy, which differs in being placed on the users' side.
choiceNotes: This describes a forward proxy. It is placed on the users' side.
This is the work of a DNS full-service resolver (caching DNS server).
Correct. It receives and relays requests in front of the servers and handles TLS processing, load distribution and the like.

web-tech-039.question: With CGI, the web server starts the program as a new process every time it receives a request, and the process ends when processing is finished. Which of the following is the main reason that FastCGI and application-server approaches can handle many requests more efficiently than CGI?
choices: Because the program's processes stay resident and are reused, the work of starting a process and initializing for each request is saved
Because they communicate with users over UDP instead of HTTP, the work of establishing a TCP connection for every request is eliminated
Because they send the program to the browser and have it run inside the browser, the server does not need to process requests
web-tech-039.explanation: CGI is a simple mechanism in which the web server passes request information to the program through environment variables and standard input, and returns what the program writes to standard output as the response. However, it starts a process for every request and redoes loading of the language runtime and connecting to the database each time, so the load becomes heavy when there are many requests. FastCGI and application servers for each language keep the program resident, connect it to the web server through sockets or similar means, and process many requests repeatedly.
choiceNotes: Correct. Keeping processes resident avoids repeating startup and initialization for every request.
FastCGI and application-server approaches also communicate with users over HTTP. The difference is how the program is run inside the server.
The program runs on the server. What runs in the browser is the JavaScript included in the page.

web-tech-040.question: Among the ways of producing the pages of a website, which of the following generates the HTML files of all pages in advance at the build stage and returns those files as they are in response to requests?
choices: CSR (client-side rendering)
SSR (server-side rendering)
SSG (static site generation)
web-tech-040.explanation: A site made with SSG is a static site that does not run a program on the server for each request, so it can be delivered quickly as is from hosting services for static files or from a CDN, and it also has fewer parts that can be attacked. For example, a site that generates its question and glossary pages from content data at build time and delivers them is of this kind, and when the content changes, the pages are generated again. SSR is a dynamic method in which the server builds HTML for each request, and CSR sends minimal HTML and JavaScript and assembles the page inside the browser.
choiceNotes: CSR is a method in which the browser runs JavaScript to assemble the page.
SSR is a method in which the server generates HTML for each request.
Correct. The HTML is generated at build time, and delivery just returns files.
